module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Squares of double factorials

Squares of double factorials: $a(n) = ((2n-1)!!)^2 = (1 \cdot 3 \cdot 5 \cdots (2n-1))^2$.

*References:*
- [A001818](https://oeis.org/A001818)
- [She, Sun, Xia, *A novel permanent identity with applications*, Theorem 1.3(ii)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.12167)
- [Yang, Zhang, *Sun-type determinant and permanent congruences*, Proposition 17](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.19502)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace OeisA1818

/-- The sequence of squares of double factorials: $a(n) = ((2n-1)!!)^2$. -/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (∏ k ∈ Finset.range n, (2 * k + 1)) ^ 2

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 0. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_0 : a 0 = 1 := by decide

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 1. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 1 := by decide

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 2. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 9 := by decide

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 3. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = 225 := by decide

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 4. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = 11025 := by decide

/-- Characteristic function $f(j, k)$ for matrix entries in $\mathbb{Z}/p^2\mathbb{Z}$. -/
noncomputable def fEntry {p : ℕ} (i j : ℕ) : ZMod (p ^ 2) :=
  let R := ZMod (p ^ 2)
  if i = j then
    1
  else
    let iInt : ℤ := i
    let jInt : ℤ := j
    let num : R := (iInt + jInt : ℤ)
    let den : R := (iInt - jInt : ℤ)
    num * den⁻¹

/--
Conjecture 1: For any primitive $2n$-th root $\zeta$ of unity, the permanent of the $2n \times 2n$
matrix $[m(j,k)]_{j,k=1..2n}$ coincides with $a(n) = ((2n-1)!!)^2$, where $m(j,k)$ is
$(1+\zeta^{j-k})/(1-\zeta^{j-k})$ if $j \neq k$, and $1$ otherwise.
- Zhi-Wei Sun, Dec 21 2021
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11 15]
theorem conjecture1 (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    ∀ (ζ : ℂ), IsPrimitiveRoot ζ (2 * n) →
      Matrix.permanent (fun (i j : Fin (2 * n)) =>
        if i = j then
          (1 : ℂ)
        else
          (1 + ζ ^ (i.val - j.val : ℤ)) / (1 - ζ ^ (i.val - j.val : ℤ))
      ) = (a n : ℂ) := by
  sorry

/--
Conjecture 2: Let $p$ be an odd prime. Then the permanent of the $(p-1) \times (p-1)$ matrix
$[f(j,k)]_{j,k=1..p-1}$ is congruent to $a((p-1)/2) = ((p-2)!!)^2 \pmod{p^2}$,
where $f(j,k)$ is $(j+k)/(j-k)$ if $j \neq k$, and $f(j,k) = 1$ otherwise.
- Zhi-Wei Sun, Dec 22 2021
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11 15]
theorem conjecture2 {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (h_odd : p ≠ 2) :
    let N : ℕ := p - 1
    let R := ZMod (p ^ 2)
    let Idx := Fin N
    let M : Matrix Idx Idx R := fun i j => fEntry (i.val + 1) (j.val + 1)
    (M.permanent : R) = (a ((p - 1) / 2) : R) := by
  sorry

end OeisA1818

findings.description: The module docstring cites Yang–Zhang as "Proposition 17" and links the unversioned abstract https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.19502, which now serves v3. In v3 the result used for `conjecture2` (per(I_{p-1}+R_p) ≡ ((p-2)!!)^2 mod p^2) is Proposition 18 (and part of Theorem 3). Number 17 in v3 is Lemma 17, Morley's congruence ((p-2)!!)^2 ≡ χ_p 2^{p-1}(p-1)! mod p^2. The number 17 is correct only for v1, where one fewer remark comes before it. The mathematics is not affected.
findings.source_evidence: arXiv:2605.19502 has versions v1 (19 May 2026), v2 and v3 (27 May 2026). v1 HTML (https://arxiv.org/html/2605.19502v1): "Proposition 17. For every odd prime p, per(I_{p-1}+R_p) ≡ ((p-2)!!)^2 (mod p^2)." In the v3 LaTeX source, theorem, proposition, lemma and remark share one counter, and v3 adds a numbered "Relation with previous work" remark (6). That makes prop:SSX 16, lem:Morley-form 17 and prop:perIRp 18.
findings.suggested_fix: Cite "Proposition 18 (Theorem 3)", or pin the link to v1: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.19502v1, Proposition 17.

reformulations.difference: The source states a congruence mod p^2 between the rational permanent of [(j+k)/(j-k)] (diagonal entries 1, j,k = 1..p-1) and ((p-2)!!)^2. The Lean instead computes each entry in ZMod (p^2) as (i+j)·(i-j)⁻¹, using ZMod's gcd-based inverse (`fEntry`), and asserts equality in ZMod (p^2) with the cast of a((p-1)/2).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For 1 ≤ i ≠ j ≤ p-1 we have 0 < |i-j| ≤ p-2, so p ∤ (i-j) and i-j is a unit mod p^2. ZMod's `⁻¹` is therefore the true inverse, and its junk value for non-units is never reached. So fEntry(i,j) is the image of (i+j)/(i-j) ∈ ℤ_(p) under the ring hom φ : ℤ_(p) → ℤ/p²ℤ. φ commutes with the sums and products defining the permanent, so the Lean LHS is φ(per). Since ker φ = p²ℤ_(p), φ(per) = φ(((p-2)!!)^2) holds iff per ≡ ((p-2)!!)^2 (mod p^2). Also a((p-1)/2) = (1·3···(p-2))^2 = ((p-2)!!)^2. Checks run: Mathlib's Matrix.permanent on a computable copy of fEntry, equal to it by rfl, gives a((p-1)/2) in ZMod(p^2) for p = 3, 5, 7; a subset-DP permanent confirms p = 11, 13, 17, 19; native_decide closes the literal statement for p = 5 and p = 7. The p ≠ 2 hypothesis follows the OEIS; Sun's original 'any prime' version is trivial at p = 2.

reformulations.difference: The Lean indexes the 2n×2n matrix by Fin (2n) = {0,…,2n-1}, with exponent (i:ℤ)-(j:ℤ); the source uses j,k = 1..2n. By contrast, conjecture2 shifts its indices by +1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Each entry depends only on the index difference: (1+ζ^{j-k})/(1-ζ^{j-k}) off the diagonal, 1 on it. Shifting both indices by 1 therefore gives the identical matrix and the same permanent. The exponent elaborates as integer subtraction ↑i.val - ↑j.val (checked with #print), so no truncated ℕ subtraction occurs. For i ≠ j, 0 < |i-j| < 2n and ζ is a primitive 2n-th root, so denominators are nonzero. `hn : 1 ≤ n` matches 'n a positive integer'. The statement is She–Sun–Xia Thm 1.3(ii) with their n = 2m. Numerically confirmed for n = 1..6 at every primitive root; the n = 1 instance was proved in Lean (the matrix is the identity).

https://arxiv.org/e-print/2605.19502 (Yang, Zhang, Sun-type determinant and permanent congruences — v3 LaTeX source, Theorem 3, Propositions 16/18)

review.notes:
No mathematical defects found. Both theorems state the source claims faithfully, and the `research solved` tags match the OEIS note (Andrew R. Epstein, Jul 16 2026) that Conjecture 1 was proved by She–Sun–Xia (2022) and Conjecture 2 by Yang–Zhang (2026). Two docstring details that do not affect the mathematics:
(1) The theorem docstrings attribute the conjectures to "Zhi-Wei Sun, Dec 21 2021" and "Dec 22 2021". The OEIS entry shows "From Zhi-Wei Sun, Jun 26 2022", both in the Sep 2022 and the Sep 2026 Wayback snapshots. The OEIS history page is behind Cloudflare and has no usable archive, so I could not tell whether an earlier edit carried the Dec 2021 dates. I therefore did not report this as a finding.
(2) The `fEntry` docstring calls it a "characteristic function"; it is really the entry function f(j,k). This is wording only.
The fixed test values a_0..a_4 (1, 1, 9, 225, 11025) match the OEIS data. Scratch files are in /workspace/review/ (numerics*.lean).
